The church has a crucifix.
She wore a crucifix.

more.def: A cross with a figure of Jesus on it, used as a symbol in some Christian churches and homes.
examples: A crucifix hung on the wall of the church.
She wore a small gold crucifix on a chain.
Many Christians keep a crucifix at home.

easy.def: Simple and rough, not finished well.
examples: He made a crude boat.
A crude drawing.
The table was crude.

more.def: Made in a simple, rough way, without much care or skill.
examples: He built a crude raft out of logs and rope.
She drew a crude map of the island with a stick in the sand.
The crude shelter kept off the wind but not the rain.

easy.def: Natural and not cleaned yet, like oil straight from the ground.
examples: Crude oil is black.
The crude oil came out of the ground.
Crude oil is thick and sticky.

more.def: In its natural state, before it has been cleaned or made into something else.
examples: Crude oil is a thick black liquid that comes out of the ground.
Workers pump crude oil from deep wells.
Crude oil is cleaned in a factory to make gasoline.

easy.def: Mean and hurting others on purpose.
examples: It is cruel to hurt animals.
The cruel king was unkind.
That was a cruel thing to say.

more.def: Causing pain or sadness to others on purpose, and not caring.
examples: It is cruel to hurt an animal.
The cruel king took food from the poor.
The frost was cruel to the new flowers.

easy.def: Being mean on purpose and causing hurt.
examples: Cruelty is mean.
He hated cruelty.
Kindness is the opposite of cruelty.

more.def: Behavior that causes pain or suffering to others and does not care.
examples: Cruelty to animals is wrong.
The book teaches that cruelty never wins.
She spoke out against cruelty at school.

easy.def: A trip on a big ship.
examples: We went on a cruise.
The cruise was fun.
The cruise ship is huge.

more.def: A holiday trip on a large ship that visits many places.
examples: We went on a cruise to the islands.
The cruise ship stopped at three ports.
They took a cruise down the river.

easy.def: To move along smoothly.
examples: The car cruises.
The ship cruised.
The bird cruised.

more.def: To travel along at a steady, smooth speed.
examples: The car cruised along the highway.
The eagle cruised over the valley.
The boat cruised across the bay.

easy.def: A large, fast ship.
examples: The cruiser sailed by.
A navy cruiser was in the port.
We saw a cruiser.

more.def: A large, fast ship, especially one used by a navy.
examples: A navy cruiser sailed into the harbor.
The cruiser was gray and had many guns.
We watched the cruiser leave the port at dawn.

easy.def: A tiny bit of bread, cake or cookie.
examples: There are crumbs on the table.
A crumb fell on the floor.
The birds ate the crumbs.

more.def: A tiny piece that has broken off bread, cake or cookies.
examples: There were cracker crumbs all over the floor.
The birds gathered to eat the bread crumbs we threw.
He brushed the crumbs off the table into his hand.

easy.def: To break into small pieces.
examples: The cookie crumbled.
The old wall crumbles.
The cake crumbled in my hand.

more.def: To break or fall apart into small pieces.
examples: The cookie crumbled in my hand.
The old wall slowly crumbled away.
The dry cake began to crumble when we sliced it.

easy.def: Not very good.
examples: I had a crummy day.
The food was crummy.
A crummy old chair.

more.def: Poor in quality or not nice.
examples: I had a crummy day, so I went to bed early.
The soup was crummy because it had no salt.
We stayed in a crummy old motel with broken lamps.

easy.def: To chew something that makes a noise.
examples: I crunch an apple.
The snow crunched.
She crunched the chips.

more.def: To crush or chew something hard so that it makes a noise.
examples: I crunched an apple.
The snow crunched under my boots.
She crunched the crackers.

easy.def: A loud, crackling sound.
examples: I heard a crunch.
The crunch of leaves.
The crunch was loud.

more.def: The sharp sound of something being crushed.
examples: I heard the crunch of gravel.
The apple had a loud crunch.
We heard a crunch as the car ran over a twig.

easy.def: A long, strong effort to make something better.
examples: She led a crusade to clean the park.
The class began a crusade for a new playground.
His crusade was to save the old tree.

more.def: A long, hard-working effort by people to change something they believe is important.
examples: The students started a crusade to keep the river clean.
Her crusade for safer streets lasted for many years.
The doctor led a crusade to get clean water to every village.

easy.def: To squash something.
examples: Do not crush the can.
The rock crushed the box.
She crushed the leaves.

more.def: To press something so hard that it is broken or flattened.
examples: The truck crushed the empty can.
She crushed the leaves in her hand.
Be careful not to crush the flowers.

easy.def: The hard outside part of bread or pie.
examples: I like the crust on my pizza.
The crust is crunchy.
He cut the crust off.

more.def: The hard outer part of bread, pie or pizza.
examples: I like the crunchy crust on my pizza.
He cut the crust off his sandwich.
The apple pie had a golden brown crust.

easy.def: The hard outer layer of something, like the Earth.
examples: The Earth has a crust.
A crust of ice formed on the pond.
The crust is hard.

more.def: The hard outer layer of something, such as the top layer of the Earth.
examples: The Earth's crust is made of solid rock.
A thin crust of ice formed on the pond overnight.
Volcanoes burst through the crust of the Earth.

easy.def: A stick that helps you walk when your leg is hurt.
examples: He walks with a crutch.
She has two crutches.
The crutch helped me walk.

more.def: A stick that fits under the arm and helps a person walk when a leg or foot is hurt.
examples: After he twisted his ankle, he used crutches to get around school.
She leaned her crutch against the wall while she sat down.
The nurse showed me how to walk with the crutches.

easy.def: To have tears come from your eyes.
examples: The baby cries.
I cried when I fell.
She cried at the sad movie.

more.def: To let tears fall from your eyes because you are sad, hurt or very happy.
examples: The baby cried until Mom picked her up.
She cried happy tears when her dog came home.
I cried when I scraped my knee on the sidewalk.

easy.def: To call out loudly.
examples: "Help!" she cried.
"Look!" he cried.
The gull cried over the sea.

more.def: To shout something out loudly.
examples: "Look out!" cried the lifeguard.
"Hooray!" cried the children as the circus began.
Gulls cried overhead as the boat came to shore.

easy.def: A hard, clear, shiny stone.
examples: The crystal sparkles.
I found a crystal.
The crystal looks like ice.

more.def: A hard, clear mineral with flat sides that shines in the light.
examples: The crystal sparkled in the sunlight.
We found a purple crystal in the cave.
Salt forms tiny crystals.
